T-001.threat: Physical boundary tampering — unauthorized physical access to boundary interior
T-001.cause: No tamper detection mechanism — unauthorized opening is undetected
T-001.attack: Attacker opens the enclosure without triggering any alarm, gaining access to internal components

T-002.threat: Debug interface physically accessible — direct hardware attack surface exposed
T-002.cause: Debug port is reachable from boundary exterior without disassembly
T-002.attack: Attacker attaches a debug probe and gains full processor access

T-003.threat: Removable media insertion — unauthorized data exfiltration or malware injection via physical media
T-003.cause: Removable media port is physically accessible — no software or physical blocking
T-003.attack: Attacker inserts a USB drive containing malware or uses it to exfiltrate sensitive data

T-004.threat: Device removal or depot attack — portable device taken for lab analysis
T-004.cause: Device is portable — attacker can control attack environment with lab equipment
T-004.attack: Attacker removes the device and performs full hardware analysis including chip-off or fault injection

I-005.threat: Side-channel observation — sensitive data extracted via physical measurements
I-005.cause: Physical boundary provides no electromagnetic shielding — internal operations are observable
I-005.attack: Attacker measures power consumption or EM emissions and extracts cryptographic keys

I-006.threat: Data exfiltration via removable media — sensitive data copied out of device
I-006.cause: Removable media port accessible — no data loss prevention mechanism
I-006.attack: Attacker inserts removable media and copies sensitive files or cryptographic material

D-007.threat: Physical destruction or power disruption — device rendered unavailable by physical attack
D-007.cause: No physical protection or anchoring — device can be damaged, unplugged, or destroyed
D-007.attack: Attacker physically damages the device or cuts power, causing immediate loss of availability

D-008.threat: Device theft — portable device stolen, causing DoS and potential data exposure
D-008.cause: Device is portable and not anchored — theft directly causes loss of availability
D-008.attack: Attacker steals the portable device causing the controlled system to lose its controller

S-008.threat: Physical boundary identity spoofing — attacker impersonates authorized personnel to gain physical access
S-008.cause: Physical access control relies on single-factor authentication — no second factor prevents impersonation
S-008.attack: Attacker impersonates an authorized person (e.g. maintenance technician) to gain physical access to the boundary interior

S-009.threat: Maintenance impersonation or relay attack — attacker gains physical access by bypassing access control
S-009.cause: Physical access control is single-factor — badge-only access is vulnerable to relay attack
S-009.attack: Attacker clones RFID badge or tailgates through controlled entry

E-010.threat: Physical privilege escalation — attacker gains elevated system access via physical boundary breach
E-010.cause: Physical access to device interior grants debug/hardware access — logical security can be bypassed
E-010.attack: Attacker opens the physical boundary and connects to internal debug interface, bypassing all software authentication

E-011.threat: Debug interface privilege escalation — full processor control via physically accessible debug port
E-011.cause: JTAG or SWD port is accessible from boundary exterior — provides full read/write access
E-011.attack: Attacker connects debug probe, halts processor, reads security keys and modifies execution flow

R-012.threat: Physical access without audit trail — actions at physical boundary cannot be attributed
R-012.cause: No physical monitoring or access logging at boundary — who accessed it and when is unknown
R-012.attack: Attacker accesses boundary and performs actions without any record being created

I-013.threat: Power side-channel attack — cryptographic key extracted via differential power analysis
I-013.cause: No power analysis countermeasures on chip — key-correlated power signature is measurable
I-013.attack: Attacker captures power traces during cryptographic operations and recovers the secret key via DPA

I-014.threat: Electromagnetic side-channel attack — sensitive data extracted via near-field EM emission
I-014.cause: No electromagnetic shielding on chip — internal operations emit correlated EM signals
I-014.attack: Attacker positions a near-field EM probe close to the chip and captures emission traces to recover key material

I-015.threat: Timing side-channel attack — secret key inferred from execution timing variations
I-015.cause: Cryptographic implementation uses data-dependent branches — execution time varies with key values
I-015.attack: Attacker measures cryptographic operation durations and applies statistical timing analysis to recover the key

I-016.threat: Physical bus probing — data extracted by probing PCB traces
I-016.cause: Security-critical bus traces exposed on PCB surface without potting or conformal coating
I-016.attack: Attacker opens the device and attaches micro-probes to exposed bus traces to capture plaintext data

I-017.threat: On-board bus eavesdropping — plaintext data captured from exposed PCB traces
I-017.cause: Data flow runs on exposed on-board traces without physical protection or encryption
I-017.attack: Attacker opens the device enclosure and attaches a logic analyzer to bus traces
